Agencies issue joint statement on third-party risk management

Published 2026-10-05 14:30 UTC

Federal bank regulatory agencies on Monday issued a joint statement clarifying their expectations for how banks manage risks arising from partnerships with financial technology companies. The statement was issued by the Federal Reserve Board, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

Many banks offer deposit accounts, payments and lending products through arrangements in which a fintech company manages the customer relationship while the bank holds the accounts. The agencies said these arrangements can expand access to financial services but also present risks if the bank does not maintain adequate oversight.

The statement highlights several areas of concern identified during examinations. These include incomplete records of customer balances held through intermediaries, weak monitoring of compliance with consumer protection laws, and insufficient planning for what happens if a partner company fails or ends the relationship.

The agencies emphasized that a bank remains responsible for compliance with all applicable laws regardless of whether activities are performed by a third party. Banks are expected to conduct due diligence before entering a partnership, monitor the partner's performance on an ongoing basis, and ensure that contracts give the bank access to the information it needs.

The statement also notes that a bank's board of directors should understand the scale of its third-party relationships and receive regular reports on related risks. Banks with large or complex fintech partnerships should consider whether their staffing, systems and capital are adequate for those activities.

The joint statement does not create new requirements but describes how existing guidance applies. The agencies said they will continue to monitor developments in bank and fintech partnerships and may issue additional guidance. The full text of the statement is attached.

The agencies invited banks and industry groups to share feedback on the statement and on areas where further clarification would be helpful. They also noted that community banks may scale their risk management practices to the size and complexity of their partnerships.
